name_reason: Already fully compliant: data_fd2_battle_ prefix (battle core table), summon_anim_variant_b domain descriptor matches its sole consumer fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_b_6slot, '10color' is a real domain dimension (array length 10 = 10 color phases, indexed by a mod-10 color_idx; NOT a Ghidra address residue), 'y_offset_table' reflects both the data shape (table/array) and semantics (per-color vertical pixel offset). No hex address suffix; the '_b' is the A/B variant letter, not a hex residue.
purpose: Read-only per-color vertical pixel offset table (10 color phases) for the variant-B summon-spell animation; selects a slot's screen-y as origin_y + y_offset[color].
logic_summary: Const int32[10] in .object2 (rodata). Sole consumer fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_b_6slot @ 0x26BFD copies the whole table to a stack-local int[10] (MOV ECX,0xA / REP MOVSD), then for each animated slot computes screen y = origin_y + y_offset[color_idx]. For the enemy team (runtime_char[caster].bTeam == 0) every entry of the LOCAL copy is biased by +0x8F before use, so the global itself is never written. Holds identical data to the variant-A table @ 0x524A8 but is a distinct symbol read by a distinct consumer (fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_a_6slot @ 0x269D3).
element_semantics: Each element [color] = vertical pixel offset (added to origin_y) for that color phase of the variant-B summon animation. Values (LE) = {30,50,70,40,80,100,70,30,60,90}. All 10 elements live (color index rotates mod 10).
comment_original_issue: Original src comment was accurate but omitted the consumer-side mechanism (whole-table copy to a stack-local and the enemy-team +0x8F bias applied in that local copy) that the parallel variant-A comment documents and that explains why the global stays read-only.
notes: Verified zero game-side write-xrefs (only READ from 0x26c1c +0/+4 and a DATA base-pointer ref from 0x26c17); .object2 block is non-writable -> is_const=true. Datatype confirmed via Ghidra Listing: int[10], len=40. Ghidra data plate was null; created a concise plate via PLATE_COMMENT. Stage-2 will handle any rename (none needed here).
